title: Seventh Word Conclusion Counsel On Prayer Avoiding Major Sins Listening To The Quran And Supplication

questions.question: What is the first main thing asked from Allah in this dua?
questions.answer: It asks Allah to fill the hearts of the believers with the light of faith and the Qur’an.

questions.question: In this passage, what kind of richness is asked for?
questions.answer: A richness that comes from knowing our need for Allah.

questions.question: What kind of poverty is the speaker asking Allah to protect people from?
questions.answer: The poverty of acting as if they do not need Allah.

questions.question: What does the dua teach about human strength and Allah’s strength?
questions.answer: It teaches that people should not depend on their own power but should turn to Allah’s power.

questions.question: Which quality toward Allah is requested after asking for refuge in His power?
questions.answer: Trusting in Allah is requested.

questions.question: What danger is mentioned when the dua says not to leave us to ourselves?
questions.answer: The danger is being left to our own weak selves instead of being guided and helped by Allah.

questions.question: Besides mercy for the speaker, who else is included in the prayer for mercy?
questions.answer: All believing men and women are included.

questions.question: Which Prophet is specially mentioned for blessings and peace?
questions.answer: Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.

questions.question: How is the Prophet described in his relationship to Allah at the start of those praises?
questions.answer: He is described as Allah’s servant, prophet, friend, and beloved.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Prophet’s role in guidance?
questions.answer: It presents him as a source of guidance and a means through which truth is shown to people.

questions.question: What does the passage show about the Prophet’s connection to Allah’s signs and names?
questions.answer: It shows him as someone who explains Allah’s signs and announces the treasures of Allah’s names.

questions.question: According to the dua, for whom was the Prophet sent as mercy?
questions.answer: He was sent as mercy for all the worlds.

questions.question: After mentioning the Prophet, which groups also receive prayers?
questions.answer: His family, his companions, the other prophets and messengers, the angels, and the righteous servants of Allah.

questions.question: What does the ending word “Ameen” show about the whole passage?
questions.answer: It shows that this is a prayer asking Allah to accept these requests.

questions.question: What two sources are asked to bring light to the heart?
questions.answer: Faith and the Qur’an.

questions.question: How does the passage connect honor with needing Allah?
questions.answer: It shows needing Allah as a kind of true richness, not a weakness.

questions.question: Why is feeling independent from Allah described in a negative way?
questions.answer: Because it makes a person spiritually poor and cut off from the real source of help.

questions.question: What change in attitude does the dua ask for regarding personal ability?
questions.answer: It asks people to stop relying on themselves and to seek help from Allah’s power.

questions.question: What does asking to be among those who trust Allah suggest about good believers?
questions.answer: It suggests that good believers place their confidence in Allah.

questions.question: What is being requested by the words asking for Allah’s protection?
questions.answer: Safety and care from Allah.

questions.question: What does the prayer for believing men and women teach about concern for others?
questions.answer: It teaches believers to care not only for themselves but for the whole Muslim community.

questions.question: In this passage, is the Prophet mentioned only by name, or also by many honorable descriptions?
questions.answer: He is mentioned with many honorable descriptions.

questions.question: What do those many descriptions of the Prophet help show?
questions.answer: They help show his high rank and his special mission.

questions.question: How is the Prophet connected to mercy in the passage?
questions.answer: He is described as an example of mercy and as one sent with mercy to all creation.

questions.question: How is the Prophet connected to teaching?
questions.answer: He is described as one who teaches Allah’s servants.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Prophet’s role in explaining divine messages?
questions.answer: It says he explains Allah’s signs and makes them understood.

questions.question: Which unseen beings are included in the closing prayers?
questions.answer: The angels are included.

questions.question: What blessing is asked for the hearts at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: Spiritual light through iman and the Qur’an.

questions.question: What does the dua say is better than acting self-sufficient?
questions.answer: Feeling one’s need for Allah is better.

questions.question: What does the prayer ask Allah to remove from us in a spiritual sense?
questions.answer: Trust in our own power and ability.

questions.question: What does it ask Allah to replace that with?
questions.answer: Refuge in Allah’s strength and power.

questions.question: What important quality of worship is requested when the dua asks to make us among those who trust Him?
questions.answer: Tawakkul, or trusting Allah.

questions.question: What can we infer about the human self from the request not to be left to ourselves?
questions.answer: We can infer that the human self is weak and needs Allah’s help.

questions.question: Who are included in the prayer for mercy besides the person making the dua?
questions.answer: All believing men and all believing women.

questions.question: What is one way the passage honors Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him?
questions.answer: It calls him Allah’s beloved messenger and gives many noble titles for his mission.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the Prophet’s place among created beings?
questions.answer: It presents him as highly honored among creation.

questions.question: What does calling him an interpreter of the signs suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that he helps people understand Allah’s messages.

questions.question: What does calling him a teacher of the servants suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that he guides people in learning and living Allah’s religion.

questions.question: What does the phrase about mercy to all the worlds tell us about the Prophet’s mission?
questions.answer: It tells us his mission was broad, merciful, and for all creation.

questions.question: Name two groups besides the Prophet who are remembered with blessings or prayers near the end.
questions.answer: His family and companions.

questions.question: What is the structure of this passage mostly made of: commands to people, a story, or supplication to Allah?
questions.answer: It is mostly supplication to Allah.

questions.question: What is the central theme of the opening lines of this passage?
questions.answer: Asking Allah for spiritual help and guidance.

questions.question: What kind of “light” is requested here?
questions.answer: Inner spiritual light, not physical light.

questions.question: How does the passage describe true enrichment?
questions.answer: True enrichment is being in need of Allah.

questions.question: How does it describe false enrichment?
questions.answer: False enrichment is thinking one has no need for Allah.

questions.question: What does the dua say believers should do with their own power and strength?
questions.answer: They should turn away from depending on it.

questions.question: In contrast, whose power should they seek?
questions.answer: Allah’s power.

questions.question: What does the request not to be left to ourselves tell us about self-reliance without Allah?
questions.answer: It shows that self-reliance alone is unsafe and not enough.

questions.question: What two large groups within the Muslim community are directly mentioned in the prayer for mercy?
questions.answer: Believing men and believing women.

questions.question: What does the passage ask Allah to send upon Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him?
questions.answer: Blessings and peace.

questions.question: How do the many titles of the Prophet affect the tone of the dua?
questions.answer: They make the dua full of respect, love, and honor.

questions.question: What role of the Prophet is highlighted by descriptions related to proof, signs, and guidance?
questions.answer: His role in showing truth and guiding people to Allah.

questions.question: What role is highlighted by descriptions related to teaching and announcing?
questions.answer: His role in delivering and explaining Allah’s message.

questions.question: Which righteous groups besides prophets are included at the end?
questions.answer: The close angels and the righteous servants of Allah.

questions.question: Why is “Ameen” a fitting ending for this passage?
questions.answer: Because the whole passage is a heartfelt prayer asking Allah to accept it.

questions.question: What does the passage ask Allah to do for the hearts of believers?
questions.answer: To brighten them with the light of belief and the Qur’an.

questions.question: What does the prayer show about the relationship between a servant and Allah?
questions.answer: It shows that the servant needs Allah completely.

questions.question: According to the dua, what is spiritually harmful: neediness before Allah or feeling independent from Him?
questions.answer: Feeling independent from Him is spiritually harmful.

questions.question: What is meant by asking to be freed from our own power and strength?
questions.answer: It means not trusting ourselves as if we are enough on our own.

questions.question: What is meant by asking to take refuge in Allah’s power and strength?
questions.answer: It means seeking help, support, and safety from Allah.

questions.question: What character trait is directly requested by asking to be among those who trust Allah?
questions.answer: Reliance on Allah.

questions.question: What does the prayer for protection suggest about Allah’s care?
questions.answer: It suggests that real protection comes from Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage balance personal prayer and community prayer?
questions.answer: It asks for help for the speaker and also for all believing men and women.

questions.question: What are some of the Prophet’s honored roles mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: He is described as a prophet, messenger, beloved, teacher, and guide.

questions.question: How is the Prophet linked to Allah’s mercy in this passage?
questions.answer: He is shown as a model of mercy and as someone sent with mercy to all worlds.

questions.question: How is the Prophet linked to Allah’s signs?
questions.answer: He is described as explaining and reflecting them.

questions.question: What does the mention of family and companions show about Muslim respect?
questions.answer: It shows respect extends to those close to the Prophet as well.

questions.question: What does including other prophets and messengers teach about Islam?
questions.answer: It teaches respect for all of Allah’s prophets.

questions.question: At the start of the passage, what two things are connected with light?
questions.answer: Iman and the Qur’an.

questions.question: What does the dua present as a better condition than worldly independence?
questions.answer: Being aware of our need for Allah.

questions.question: What negative spiritual state does the dua ask Allah to keep away from us?
questions.answer: Thinking we do not need Allah.

questions.question: What two human qualities are set aside before seeking Allah’s help?
questions.answer: One’s own strength and one’s own power.

questions.question: After turning away from self-power, what does the dua ask believers to hold onto?
questions.answer: Allah’s strength and power.

questions.question: What does being counted among those who trust Allah tell us about an ideal Muslim attitude?
questions.answer: An ideal Muslim depends on Allah with confidence.

questions.question: Why does the dua ask not to be entrusted to ourselves?
questions.answer: Because people are weak and can go wrong without Allah’s care.

questions.question: Who receives a prayer for mercy in the middle of the passage?
questions.answer: The speaker and all believing men and women.

questions.question: What does the passage ask Allah to send on Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him?
questions.answer: Blessings and peace.

questions.question: What is one idea repeated through the many titles of the Prophet?
questions.answer: He has a noble mission of guidance, mercy, and explaining truth.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the Prophet’s importance in understanding Allah’s signs?
questions.answer: It suggests he helps people recognize and understand them.

questions.question: What broadness of mission is shown by saying he was sent as mercy to all the worlds?
questions.answer: His mission reaches beyond one group and is for all creation.

questions.question: Which groups are prayed for after the Prophet is mentioned?
questions.answer: His family, companions, fellow prophets and messengers, angels, and righteous servants.

questions.question: What is the best overall description of this whole target passage?
questions.answer: It is a dua full of humility, trust in Allah, and love and honor for the Prophet and the believers.
